functions.funcDef: Provide propulsive thrust for all phases of flight (PRP §5.1.1).

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to provide control authority across the envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (FCS §5.3.1).
functions.subDef: Two-segment ailerons and multi-function spoilers position for roll control (§5.3.2).

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to provide control authority across the envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (FCS §5.3.1).
functions.subDef: All-moving trimmable horizontal stabiliser with elevators positions for pitch control (§5.3.2).

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to provide control authority across the envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (FCS §5.3.1).
functions.subDef: Split rudder in upper and lower segments, each with own actuation and hydraulic supply, sizes the engine-out directional case (§5.3.2, §5.3.3).

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to provide control authority across the envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (FCS §5.3.1).
functions.subDef: Double-slotted Fowler flaps in four sections and full-span leading-edge slats, driven by two PDUs through a common torque shaft with asymmetry brakes (§5.3.2).

functions.funcName: Support and control aircraft on the ground
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on the ground, absorb landing/taxi loads, provide braking and ground directional control on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces (LDG §5.6.1).
functions.subName: Support aircraft and absorb ground loads
functions.subDef: Nose unit and six main bogies support the aircraft and absorb landing and taxi loads, spreading footprint pressure for semi-prepared surfaces (§5.6.1, §5.6.2).

functions.funcName: Support and control aircraft on the ground
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on the ground, absorb landing/taxi loads, provide braking and ground directional control on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces (LDG §5.6.1).
functions.subDef: Hydraulic retraction/extension on system A with free-fall alternate; uplocks/downlocks mechanically held, hydraulically released (§5.6.2).

functions.funcName: Support and control aircraft on the ground
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on the ground, absorb landing/taxi loads, provide braking and ground directional control on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces (LDG §5.6.1).
functions.subDef: Carbon multi-disc braking, normally system B with system A alternate and accumulator-supported emergency braking; anti-skid per wheel pair (§5.6.2).

functions.funcName: Support and control aircraft on the ground
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on the ground, absorb landing/taxi loads, provide braking and ground directional control on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces (LDG §5.6.1).
functions.subDef: Hydraulic nose-wheel steering commanded from tillers and rudder pedals, with mechanical disconnect for towing (§5.6.2).

functions.funcName: Provide cargo access and pressure boundary at nose
functions.funcDef: Provide straight-in nose access to the hold and, when closed, form part of the pressure boundary (NZD §5.7.1). Structural load-path role of the door is treated as structure, not function (§5.7.3).
functions.subDef: Upward-hinging visor opened/closed hydraulically from system A with electric backup drive; cannot be operated in flight (§5.7.2, §5.7.6).

functions.funcName: Provide cargo access and pressure boundary at nose
functions.funcDef: Provide straight-in nose access to the hold and, when closed, form part of the pressure boundary (NZD §5.7.1). Structural load-path role of the door is treated as structure, not function (§5.7.3).
functions.subDef: Twelve rotary latches on a common torque shaft plus eight locking pins on a separate supply; pressure interlock in series with unlock (§5.7.2).

functions.funcName: Provide cargo access and pressure boundary at nose
functions.funcDef: Provide straight-in nose access to the hold and, when closed, form part of the pressure boundary (NZD §5.7.1). Structural load-path role of the door is treated as structure, not function (§5.7.3).
functions.subDef: Two dissimilar independently routed circuits sense lock; status displayed on flight deck and fed to take-off configuration monitor (§5.7.2, §5.7.4).

functions.funcDef: Receive, position and restrain a single blade and maintain restraint through all flight and ground load cases (CRG §5.8.1). Hold floor hard points are structure, not function (§5.8.3).
functions.subDef: Longitudinal restraint by two tension straps per saddle, tensioned by electric winches and locked mechanically; lateral/vertical by saddle geometry (§5.8.2).

functions.funcDef: Receive, position and restrain a single blade and maintain restraint through all flight and ground load cases (CRG §5.8.1). Hold floor hard points are structure, not function (§5.8.3).
functions.subDef: Single instrumented tension loop; loss of tension on any strap annunciated in flight, two adjacent stations flagged as restraint condition (§5.8.2).

functions.funcDef: Condition and distribute air to the flight deck and hold, and control fuselage pressure differential (ECS §5.9.1).
functions.subDef: Two air cycle packs on cross-bleed condition and distribute air to two separate zones, flight deck and hold (§5.9.2).

functions.funcDef: Condition and distribute air to the flight deck and hold, and control fuselage pressure differential (ECS §5.9.1).
functions.subDef: Two digital controllers driving two outflow valves with pneumatic backup; independent positive/negative mechanical relief protects the structure (§5.9.2).

functions.funcDef: Prevent or remove ice accretion on surfaces, inlets and probes for flight in the icing envelope (IPS §5.10.1).
functions.subName: Protect aerodynamic surfaces and inlets from ice
functions.subDef: Hot bleed air protects wing leading edges and engine inlet cowls; stabiliser leading edges electrically heated in six independent zones (§5.10.2).

functions.funcDef: Prevent or remove ice accretion on surfaces, inlets and probes for flight in the icing envelope (IPS §5.10.1).
functions.subName: Protect probes and windshields from ice
functions.subDef: Probes, static ports, windshields and two ice detectors electrically heated and monitored individually (§5.10.2).

functions.funcDef: Prevent or remove ice accretion on surfaces, inlets and probes for flight in the icing envelope (IPS §5.10.1).
functions.subDef: Two ice detectors of the same type on opposite sides of the forward fuselage provide advisory detection and automatic activation (§5.10.2).

functions.funcName: Provide flight-crew information and control interface
functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and host the alerting (AVI §5.11.1).
functions.subDef: Four display units and two head-up displays driven by three display processors on dual networks; any unit can present any format (§5.11.2).

functions.funcName: Provide flight-crew information and control interface
functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and host the alerting (AVI §5.11.1).
functions.subName: Provide air data and inertial reference
functions.subDef: Three air data inertial reference units supply air data and inertial data, two on main buses and one on DC essential (§5.11.2).

functions.funcName: Provide flight-crew information and control interface
functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and host the alerting (AVI §5.11.1).
functions.subDef: Independent integrated standby instrument on DC essential bus, sharing no supply, sensor or processing with the primary displays (§5.11.2, §5.11.3).

functions.funcName: Provide flight-crew information and control interface
functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and host the alerting (AVI §5.11.1).
functions.subDef: Alerting system consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list with procedures, on two independent channels (§5.11.2).

functions.funcDef: Detect fire and overheat where they must be detected and provide the means to extinguish or suppress them (FPR §5.12.1).
functions.subDef: Dual-loop continuous detection per engine nacelle and APU, overheat detection on bleed duct runs and main gear bays, hold smoke detection at nine stations (§5.12.2).

functions.funcDef: Detect fire and overheat where they must be detected and provide the means to extinguish or suppress them (FPR §5.12.1).
functions.subDef: Two extinguisher bottles per engine pair cross-plumbed, independent APU bottle; hold has detection but deliberately no suppression (§5.12.2).

functions.funcDef: Supply breathing oxygen to the flight crew for loss of pressurisation, smoke and fume events, and the following descent and diversion (OXY §5.13.1).
functions.subDef: Two high-pressure cylinders on a common manifold with crossover feed four quick-donning full-face demand masks; sized for four occupants for the diversion time (§5.13.2).

fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing, Go-around
fha.effAc: Simultaneous loss of thrust from all four engines removes the ability to sustain flight; the aircraft becomes a glider and cannot achieve continued safe flight and landing — normally with hull loss.
fha.effCrew: Fatalities or incapacitation — the flight crew are aboard and the outcome is not recoverable by crew action once all thrust is lost.
fha.effPax: Multiple fatalities — occupants (flight crew only; hold unoccupied) do not survive the hull loss.
fha.comments: ⚠ PHASES DROPPED — the model named Initial climb, not in this project's phase table; exposure is computed without them. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of all thrust prevents continued safe flight and landing, which "would result in multiple fatalities, usually with the loss of the airplane", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.5. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] Levels: Aircraft hull loss · Crew fatalities or incapacitation · Occupants multiple fatalities → Catastrophic (all three axes at the catastrophic step). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of forward thrust — symmetric
fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing, Go-around
fha.effAc: Symmetric partial loss (e.g. one engine per side, or a symmetric power reduction) leaves controllable flight with reduced climb and single-engine-out-equivalent performance; the aircraft is designed to continue to a suitable aerodrome after loss of any one engine, giving a significant reduction in functional capabilities and safety margins.
fha.effCrew: Significant increase in crew workload to manage the degraded thrust, re-plan and select a diversion; no annunciation loss assumed.
fha.effPax: Physical discomfort possible; no injuries expected for the credited symmetric case.
fha.judgementNote: Class taken as Major for a symmetric partial loss recoverable within the one-engine-inoperative dispatch case; a symmetric multi-engine loss on the same event (e.g. common bleed/fuel cause) could be Hazardous or worse. Confirm the credited extent of "partial" and rule out common-cause; FADEC/fuel-feed failure-mode data would settle it.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Class taken as Major for a symmetric partial loss recoverable within the one-engine-inoperative dispatch case; a symmetric multi-engine loss on the same event (e.g. common bleed/fuel cause) could be Hazardous or worse. Confirm the credited extent of "partial" and rule out common-cause; FADEC/fuel-feed failure-mode data would settle it. | ⚠ PHASES DROPPED — the model named Initial climb, not in this project's phase table; exposure is computed without them. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Symmetric partial thrust loss produces a "significant reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.3, with a significant increase in flightcrew workload. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] Levels: Aircraft significant · Crew significant · Occupants discomfort → Major (aircraft and crew axes govern). — engineer to confirm.

fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing, Go-around
fha.effAc: An uncommanded thrust change on one or more engines (runaway high, rollback, or asymmetry) at the 28 m outboard moment arm produces a directional/upset disturbance the crew must arrest; credited as a large reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities with the crew retaining control.
fha.effCrew: Physical distress or excessive workload to detect and counter the uncommanded thrust and directional excursion, near the limit at which the crew can be relied upon to perform accurately.
fha.effPax: Serious injury possible to a small number of occupants during the excursion; hold unoccupied.
fha.judgementNote: Credited the recoverable asymmetric-excursion outcome (crew arrests it) as Hazardous, not the unrecoverable case. Outboard-engine asymmetry is the stated directional sizing case; whether an uncommanded case can defeat rudder authority and become Catastrophic depends on FADEC overspeed/runaway failure modes and reverser behaviour — not in the SDD. FADEC and thrust-control failure-mode data would confirm or overturn the class.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Outboard-engine asymmetry is the stated directional sizing case; whether an uncommanded case can defeat rudder authority and become Catastrophic depends on FADEC overspeed/runaway failure modes and reverser behaviour — not in the SDD. FADEC and thrust-control failure-mode data would confirm or overturn the class. | ⚠ PHASES DROPPED — the model named Initial climb, not in this project's phase table; exposure is computed without them. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An uncommanded thrust change at the outboard moment arm gives a "large reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.4, with excessive crew workload to arrest the excursion. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] Levels: Aircraft large · Crew large · Occupants severe injuries or few fatalities → Hazardous (all three axes at the catastrophic step). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of forward thrust — asymmetric
fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing, Go-around
fha.effAc: Asymmetric partial loss (single outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm) is the directional-control sizing case; controllable with rudder authority carried in the flight-control sizing, with a significant reduction in climb performance and safety margins.
fha.effCrew: Significant increase in crew workload to counter the yaw/roll asymmetry, retrim and manage the diversion; within crew capability with the sized rudder authority.
fha.effPax: Physical discomfort possible; no injuries expected for the credited single-engine asymmetric case.
fha.judgementNote: Class taken as Major for the single-outboard-engine loss the aircraft is dispatched to survive with rudder authority sized to it. The SDD notes loss of a second engine on the same side is outside the design dispatch case — that combination is not this row and could be worse. Confirm the credited single-engine extent; second-same-side loss handled separately.

fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing, Go-around
fha.effAc: The aircraft delivers thrust materially different from that commanded (wrong magnitude, wrong engine, or lagged), degrading energy management and — if the error is asymmetric — introducing a directional disturbance at the outboard moment arm; credited as a large reduction in functional capabilities with the crew retaining control.
fha.effCrew: Physical distress or excessive workload to recognise the erroneous thrust response, revert to manual/alternate control and stabilise the flight path.
fha.effPax: Serious injury possible to a small number of occupants during the resulting excursion; hold unoccupied.
fha.judgementNote: Credited the recoverable erroneous-response case as Hazardous. The severity hinges on whether the error can be simultaneous across engines or defeat FADEC protection (overspeed/overtemperature are FADEC-protected without crew action per the SDD), which could raise or lower the class. FADEC channel-independence and command-error failure-mode data would confirm.

fha.phases: Landing
fha.effAc: Reverse thrust unavailable on landing rollout; deceleration relies wholly on wheel braking and spoilers against the 1,800 m landing distance requirement, with predicted rollout ~1,080 m — a reduction in stopping margin on a semi-prepared surface.
fha.effCrew: Crew apply maximum wheel braking; a slight-to-significant increase in workload managing rollout within available distance.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.judgementNote: Assumed wheel braking + spoilers hold the aircraft within the 1,800 m requirement with reversers lost. The braking-degradation assessment against the ~1,080 m predicted rollout on a semi-prepared surface would confirm Major or overturn it to Hazardous.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Assumed wheel braking + spoilers hold the aircraft within the 1,800 m requirement with reversers lost. The braking-degradation assessment against the ~1,080 m predicted rollout on a semi-prepared surface would confirm Major or overturn it to Hazardous. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Reverse thrust is supplementary deceleration; wheel braking and spoilers remain, but the loss reduces the stopping margin on a semi-prepared surface — "significant reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.3. JUDGEMENT: rests on the braking-degradation margin between 1,800 m required and ~1,080 m predicted; if that margin does not absorb reverser loss on the operating surface this may rise to Hazardous. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] Levels: Aircraft significant · Crew slight · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Major (aircraft axis governs). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of reverse thrust — asymmetric
fha.phases: Landing
fha.effAc: One inboard reverser deployed, one not, producing an asymmetric retarding force on rollout in addition to reduced total reverse; a directional disturbance combined with reduced deceleration margin on a semi-prepared surface.
fha.effCrew: Crew counter the asymmetry with steering/rudder and braking while managing stopping distance; a significant increase in workload during rollout.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.judgementNote: Assumed the crew arrest the asymmetry with steering and rudder within available runway on a semi-prepared surface. Directional-control sizing and braking-degradation analysis would confirm Major or overturn it if the excursion cannot be contained.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Assumed the crew arrest the asymmetry with steering and rudder within available runway on a semi-prepared surface. Directional-control sizing and braking-degradation analysis would confirm Major or overturn it if the excursion cannot be contained. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Asymmetric reverse introduces a controllable directional disturbance and reduced deceleration — "a significant increase in flightcrew workload", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.3, and a significant reduction in stopping margin. JUDGEMENT: rests on nose-wheel steering/rudder authority to hold the runway and the braking margin absorbing the reduced reverse. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] Levels: Aircraft significant · Crew significant · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Major (aircraft and crew axes govern). — engineer to confirm.

fha.phases: Landing, Takeoff
fha.effAc: Unintended reverser deployment on the ground produces an asymmetric or unexpected retarding force; on takeoff an inadvertent deployment during the ground roll degrades acceleration and introduces a directional disturbance requiring reject.
fha.effCrew: Crew detect the reverse annunciation/deceleration cue and reject the takeoff or manage the rollout; a significant increase in workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.judgementNote: Assumed inadvertent deployment is confined to the ground (this row) and is recoverable via reject/steering. Directional-control and rejected-takeoff performance would confirm Major.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Assumed inadvertent deployment is confined to the ground (this row) and is recoverable via reject/steering. Directional-control and rejected-takeoff performance would confirm Major. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Ground inadvertent deployment is a controllable directional/deceleration disturbance the crew can manage or reject against — "a significant increase in flightcrew workload", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.3. JUDGEMENT: rests on the excursion being contained within available runway; the in-flight case is captured separately under SF-002-M2. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] Levels: Aircraft significant · Crew significant · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Major (aircraft and crew axes govern). — engineer to confirm.

fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach
fha.effAc: Uncommanded in-flight reverse on an inboard engine produces significant thrust opposite to that commanded plus a large asymmetry at the inboard moment arm, a large reduction in directional and speed control margins requiring the sizing rudder authority to hold flight path.
fha.effCrew: Crew apply large rudder/roll input and manage the asymmetry and speed loss; physical distress or excessive workload to retain control.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.judgementNote: Assumed the FCS directional-control sizing (outboard-engine-out sizing case) leaves recoverable authority against an inboard uncommanded reverse asymmetry. The flight-control asymmetric-thrust sizing analysis would confirm Hazardous or, if control cannot be retained, drive Catastrophic.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Assumed the FCS directional-control sizing (outboard-engine-out sizing case) leaves recoverable authority against an inboard uncommanded reverse asymmetry. The flight-control asymmetric-thrust sizing analysis would confirm Hazardous or, if control cannot be retained, drive Catastrophic. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: In-flight uncommanded reverse is "significant thrust in the opposite direction to that commanded by the pilot" (AC 33.75(g)(2)(iii)) creating a large asymmetry — "a large reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.4. JUDGEMENT: the flight inhibits (WoW + radio-altimeter + mechanical sleeve lock) make this remote, but the residual failure state is classified by its effect; whether it is Hazardous or Catastrophic turns on the directional-control sizing case. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] Levels: Aircraft large · Crew large · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Hazardous (aircraft and crew axes govern). — engineer to confirm.

fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: No fuel delivered to any engine — total loss of thrust from all four engines; the aircraft cannot sustain flight and continued safe flight and landing is not possible.
fha.effCrew: Total thrust loss; the crew cannot maintain flight, hull loss.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; crew fatalities with loss of the aircraft.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of fuel delivery is loss of thrust from all four engines and prevents continued safe flight and landing — "a failure condition that would prevent continued safe flight and landing should be classified as catastrophic", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.5 Note 1. Engine-level §33.75(g)(1) minor classification does not apply at aircraft level where the condition is the simultaneous loss of all sources of thrust. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] Levels: Aircraft hull loss · Crew fatalities or incapacitation · Occupants multiple fatalities → Catastrophic (all three axes at the catastrophic step). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of fuel delivery — single engine

fha.effAc: Fuel starvation of one engine causes loss of thrust from that engine; the aircraft is designed to continue to a suitable aerodrome following loss of any one engine at or after V1, leaving three engines and a significant reduction in functional capabilities.
fha.effCrew: Crew recognise the affected-engine low-pressure discrete, action the engine-out drill and cross-feed as required, and continue to a suitable aerodrome — a significant increase in flightcrew workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). fha.effPax: Multiple fatalities.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of lock status indication

Per §5.4.2 loss of annunciation is itself a failure condition, and here it is the annunciation of a catastrophic un-secured-door condition.
fha.effCrew: Crew cannot verify lock status and must apply a dispatch/procedural constraint; significant increase in workload to establish door security by alternative means before dispatch.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; no effect.

A showing on the take-off configuration monitor and any redundant indication could move this.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of air conditioning and distribution
fha.phases: Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: No conditioned air is delivered to the flight deck or hold. With both packs lost, the aircraft cannot maintain flight-deck conditioning; combined with pressurisation this drives a descent to a breathable altitude. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] Levels: Aircraft significant · Crew significant · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Major (aircraft and crew axes govern). — engineer to confirm.

fha.phases: Taxi, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Misleading alerting the crew do not recognise as false; crew act on incorrect information, taking no corrective action against the alerting itself, potentially degrading the ability to cope with adverse conditions.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware the alert is erroneous continue normal duties and may take inappropriate action against a correct system; latent misleading information reduces their ability to manage the flight correctly.
fha.effPax: No effect on occupants; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.judgementNote: Undetected erroneous alerting: crew cannot cross-check because they do not know it is false, but primary displays and standby instrument remain independent means to reveal the true state. Classed Major; whether a specific undetected false alert could drive an unrecoverable action would be needed to raise the class.

Severity rationale: Effects support "significant reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.3; misleading un-recognised information is assessed for the crew acting on it. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] Levels: Aircraft significant · Crew significant · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Major (aircraft and crew axes govern). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fire and overheat detection
fha.phases: Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: No fire or overheat in any monitored zone (engine nacelles, APU, bleed ducts, gear bays, hold) is detected or annunciated; a fire that starts is not indicated and the crew cannot initiate the fire handles or extinguishing on time, so an uncontained fire can develop leading to a large reduction in functional capabilities.
fha.effCrew: Crew receive no fire/overheat warning and take no protective action; workload is a large reduction in the ability to cope with a fire that goes unindicated until secondary cues appear.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no passengers. Flight crew exposed to an undetected fire developing to a serious outcome.
fha.judgementNote: Assumed the fire-detection function is required and that undetected fire in an engine nacelle or APU without crew warning drives a large safety-margin reduction; the SDD gives dual-loop detection per zone but no aircraft-effect statement. A combination FHA/PRA with the fire-suppression function and exposure would confirm Hazardous vs Catastrophic.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Assumed the fire-detection function is required and that undetected fire in an engine nacelle or APU without crew warning drives a large safety-margin reduction; the SDD gives dual-loop detection per zone but no aircraft-effect statement. A combination FHA/PRA with the fire-suppression function and exposure would confirm Hazardous vs Catastrophic. | ⚠ PHASES DROPPED — the model named Taxi-out, Take-off, Taxi-in, not in this project's phase table; exposure is computed without them. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of the entire fire/overheat detection function combined with an undetected fire produces a "large reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities" (AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.4) and, per §5.4.2, loss of a required warning combined with the un-annunciated fire is assessed against the fire-event outcome; escalation to Catastrophic is credibly reachable and is a judgement to confirm against the loss-of-detection-plus-fire combination probability. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] Levels: Aircraft large · Crew large · Occupants severe injuries or few fatalities → Hazardous (all three axes at the catastrophic step). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of fire and overheat detection
fha.phases: Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Detection lost in some zones or degraded to single-loop logic while other zones remain covered; a fire in an unmonitored zone is not indicated, giving a significant reduction in functional capabilities.
fha.effCrew: Loss of coverage in some zones is annunciated; crew manage remaining coverage with a significant increase in workload monitoring the degraded state.
fha.effPax: No passengers; flight crew exposed to reduced detection coverage in the affected zone.
fha.judgementNote: Assumed partial loss means one or more zones lose detection while others retain it, and that the loss is annunciated per the dual-loop degradation described in SDD §5.12.2. Which zone is lost and whether that zone is fire-critical would confirm Major vs Hazardous.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Assumed partial loss means one or more zones lose detection while others retain it, and that the loss is annunciated per the dual-loop degradation described in SDD §5.12.2. Which zone is lost and whether that zone is fire-critical would confirm Major vs Hazardous. | ⚠ PHASES DROPPED — the model named Taxi-out, Take-off, Taxi-in, not in this project's phase table; exposure is computed without them. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of coverage in a subset of zones is a "significant reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities" (AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.3); dual-loop-to-single-loop degradation is an annunciated loss-of-annunciation case which §5.4.2 classifies Major unless shown otherwise, with the remaining zones still covered. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] Levels: Aircraft significant · Crew significant · Occupants discomfort → Major (aircraft and crew axes govern). — engineer to confirm.

fha.phases: Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Detection reports incorrect state — a real fire in one zone reported as a different zone or masked, or overheat mis-located; crew act on wrong information, a significant reduction in functional capabilities.
fha.effCrew: Crew respond to an erroneous indication (wrong engine shut down or wrong fire handle) — a significant increase in workload and potential for incorrect corrective action.
fha.effPax: No passengers; crew exposed to consequences of acting on wrong detection.
fha.judgementNote: Assumed erroneous detection can misdirect crew to shut down a healthy engine or misidentify the fire zone. Whether a mis-shutdown during a real fire escalates to Hazardous depends on the combination with an actual fire event and would confirm the class.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Assumed erroneous detection can misdirect crew to shut down a healthy engine or misidentify the fire zone. Whether a mis-shutdown during a real fire escalates to Hazardous depends on the combination with an actual fire event and would confirm the class. | ⚠ PHASES DROPPED — the model named Taxi-out, Take-off, Taxi-in, not in this project's phase table; exposure is computed without them. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous detection leading the crew to take incorrect action is a "significant reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities" with a "significant increase in flightcrew workload" (AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.3); dual-loop AND logic for warning limits nuisance escalation but misdirected crew action is credibly Major. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] Levels: Aircraft significant · Crew significant · Occupants discomfort → Major (aircraft and crew axes govern). — engineer to confirm.

fha.phases: Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: A fire/overheat warning is generated with no fire present; if the crew act on it (engine shutdown, extinguisher discharge) the aircraft loses thrust or a bottle without cause, a slight-to-significant reduction in functional capabilities depending on phase.
fha.effCrew: Crew respond to a false warning with unnecessary shutdown/discharge and diversion — a significant increase in workload managing a non-existent emergency.
fha.effPax: No passengers; crew workload increased by the false alarm and its consequences.
fha.judgementNote: Assumed crew act on the false warning (shutdown/discharge) per normal procedure; effect worst at take-off where a false-warning shutdown reduces margins. Phase-dependent effects could split this into a second row if a take-off inadvertent warning is judged Hazardous.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Assumed crew act on the false warning (shutdown/discharge) per normal procedure; effect worst at take-off where a false-warning shutdown reduces margins. Phase-dependent effects could split this into a second row if a take-off inadvertent warning is judged Hazardous. | ⚠ PHASES DROPPED — the model named Taxi-out, Take-off, Taxi-in, not in this project's phase table; exposure is computed without them. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A false fire warning driving an unnecessary engine shutdown or extinguisher discharge is a "significant increase in flightcrew workload" with a "significant reduction in ... functional capabilities" (AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.3), most severe if it occurs at take-off; dual-loop AND warning logic reduces but does not eliminate the case. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] Levels: Aircraft significant · Crew significant · Occupants discomfort → Major (aircraft and crew axes govern). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of fire and overheat detection
fha.phases: Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Detection function is lost AND the loss is itself not annunciated; the crew believe fire protection is available when it is not, so a fire that starts goes wholly unindicated with no crew action — an uncontained fire develops leading toward loss of the aircraft.
fha.effCrew: Crew take no action and continue duties believing detection is functioning; they receive no cue until the fire produces secondary effects, by which time control of the outcome may be lost.
fha.effPax: No passengers; flight crew exposed to an undetected fire with no protective response and no warning of the lost function.
fha.judgementNote: Assumed 'undetected' means the loss of the detection function is itself latent (no annunciation of the failed detection), making it a significant latent failure that, combined with a fire, would be hazardous or catastrophic. Latency exposure and the combination probability with a nacelle/APU fire would confirm Hazardous vs Catastrophic.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Assumed 'undetected' means the loss of the detection function is itself latent (no annunciation of the failed detection), making it a significant latent failure that, combined with a fire, would be hazardous or catastrophic. Latency exposure and the combination probability with a nacelle/APU fire would confirm Hazardous vs Catastrophic. | ⚠ PHASES DROPPED — the model named Taxi-out, Take-off, Taxi-in, not in this project's phase table; exposure is computed without them. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Latent loss of detection with no annunciation of the loss removes both the fire warning and the awareness of its absence; per AC 25.1309-1B §5.4.2 the combination of a failure with failure of its annunciation must meet the objective of the un-annunciated effect, and the un-annunciated fire yields a "large reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities" (§3.1.4). Escalation to Catastrophic on combination with a fire event is a judgement to confirm; this is also a significant latent failure per §25.4. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] Levels: Aircraft large · Crew large · Occupants severe injuries or few fatalities → Hazardous (all three axes at the catastrophic step). — engineer to confirm.

fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: No means to extinguish a detected engine-nacelle or APU fire; an uncontrolled fire in a nacelle or the APU compartment can propagate to the wing/fuel or structure, producing a large reduction in functional capabilities up to loss of the airplane.
fha.effCrew: Fire warning presented but the fire handle achieves no discharge; crew cannot arrest the fire by the assumed aircraft means, leaving them unable to cope with the condition.
fha.effPax: Crew-only freighter; hold unoccupied, no passengers aboard — occupant effect is realised on the flight crew as fatalities or incapacitation in the hull-loss end state.
fha.judgementNote: Assumed a nacelle/APU fire without any extinguishing can reach the wing fuel or primary structure before a diversion; the SDD states extinguishing is provided but does not bound propagation. Fire-propagation and diversion-time analysis (PRA/ZSA) would confirm or reduce this to Hazardous.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Assumed a nacelle/APU fire without any extinguishing can reach the wing fuel or primary structure before a diversion; the SDD states extinguishing is provided but does not bound propagation. Fire-propagation and diversion-time analysis (PRA/ZSA) would confirm or reduce this to Hazardous. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncontrolled in-flight fire with no extinguishing means can propagate to fuel/structure and prevent continued safe flight and landing: "A failure condition that would result in multiple fatalities, usually with the loss of the airplane", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.5. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] Levels: Aircraft hull loss · Crew fatalities or incapacitation · Occupants multiple fatalities → Catastrophic (all three axes at the catastrophic step). — engineer to confirm.

fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Extinguishing available to some but not all protected zones (e.g. one bottle of a cross-plumbed pair, or APU-only loss); a fire in the unprotected zone cannot be discharged into, giving a large reduction in functional capabilities where that zone fires, though cross-plumbing preserves coverage of the affected engine pair.
fha.effCrew: Fire warning presented; discharge achieves effect in covered zones but not in the affected one, so for a fire in that zone the crew cannot be relied upon to arrest it.
fha.effPax: Crew-only freighter, hold unoccupied; occupant effect realised on flight crew consistent with the aircraft effect in the affected zone.
fha.judgementNote: Assumed 'partial' means loss of one bottle/one zone with cross-plumbing retained per §5.12.2; the FCIM does not bound which zones lose coverage. If a partial loss can disable both bottles of a pair simultaneously the outcome approaches the SF-028-TL case.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Assumed 'partial' means loss of one bottle/one zone with cross-plumbing retained per §5.12.2; the FCIM does not bound which zones lose coverage. If a partial loss can disable both bottles of a pair simultaneously the outcome approaches the SF-028-TL case. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of extinguishing for one protected zone gives a "large reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities" for a fire in that zone, AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.4, with cross-plumbing limiting the exposure short of the all-zones catastrophic case. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] Levels: Aircraft large · Crew large · Occupants severe injuries or few fatalities → Hazardous (all three axes at the catastrophic step). — engineer to confirm.

fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Agent discharged into a nacelle or the APU compartment with no fire present; the bottle for that zone is expended, leaving that zone without extinguishing until reservicing, but no immediate reduction in airplane capability.
fha.effCrew: Unexpected discharge indication; crew workload to assess and confirm no fire, a slight increase within their capabilities, with the affected zone now unprotected as a latent consequence.
fha.effPax: Crew-only freighter, hold unoccupied; no passenger effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Inadvertent discharge causes no realised aircraft effect and "would only involve flightcrew actions that are well within their capabilities", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.2; the resulting loss of protection for that zone is captured separately by SF-028-PL. [anchor MIN-1 — Minor] Levels: Aircraft slight · Crew slight · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Minor (aircraft and crew axes govern). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of crew oxygen supply
fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: No breathing oxygen to any crew mask; the airplane retains its own capability but is dependent on a crew that cannot be protected during a loss-of-pressurisation, smoke or fume event and the descent/diversion that follows.
fha.effCrew: During a depressurisation, smoke or fume event the crew has no oxygen and cannot be relied upon to perform their tasks accurately or completely; at the low operating altitude time of useful consciousness is longer than at high altitude but a smoke/fume event still impairs the crew directly.
fha.effPax: Crew-only freighter, hold unoccupied; no passenger oxygen is fitted and none is required — occupant effect is on the flight crew only.
fha.judgementNote: Assumed the sizing case is a coincident depressurisation or smoke/fume event per §5.13.1; loss of oxygen alone in an intact cabin at FL260 or below has milder effect. If a coincident depressurisation is not credited concurrently, the standalone class may be lower; a combined pressurisation-loss FHA row would settle this.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Assumed the sizing case is a coincident depressurisation or smoke/fume event per §5.13.1; loss of oxygen alone in an intact cabin at FL260 or below has milder effect. If a coincident depressurisation is not credited concurrently, the standalone class may be lower; a combined pressurisation-loss FHA row would settle this. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of crew oxygen during the events it exists to cover leaves "physical distress or excessive workload such that the flightcrew cannot be relied upon to perform their tasks accurately or completely", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.4. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] Levels: Aircraft large · Crew large · Occupants severe injuries or few fatalities → Hazardous (all three axes at the catastrophic step). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of crew oxygen supply
fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Oxygen available but at reduced quantity/duration (one cylinder, or reduced reserve via the crossover); the airplane retains capability but the diversion duration protected is reduced, a significant reduction in the margin available for the descent/diversion after a pressurisation or smoke event.
fha.effCrew: Crew retains oxygen from the remaining cylinder through the crossover at reduced reserve; a significant increase in workload managing a shortened protected diversion time, still within their capability for the low-altitude case.
fha.effPax: Crew-only freighter, hold unoccupied; no passenger effect.
fha.judgementNote: Assumed partial loss retains one cylinder via the crossover at reduced reserve per §5.13.3; the FCIM does not quantify the reserve remaining. If a partial loss can leave insufficient oxygen for the required diversion the class approaches the SF-029-TL hazardous case.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Assumed partial loss retains one cylinder via the crossover at reduced reserve per §5.13.3; the FCIM does not quantify the reserve remaining. If a partial loss can leave insufficient oxygen for the required diversion the class approaches the SF-029-TL hazardous case. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Reduced oxygen reserve during a pressurisation or smoke event is a "significant reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.3, the crossover preserving supply short of the complete-loss hazardous case. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] Levels: Aircraft significant · Crew significant · Occupants discomfort → Major (aircraft and crew axes govern). — engineer to confirm.

fha.phases: Taxi, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: No direct effect on airplane functional capability or safety margins; the airplane systems are unaffected.
fha.effCrew: Crew breathing oxygen is delivered incorrectly (contaminated, wrong concentration or degraded flow) so that crew protection is reduced during a depressurisation, smoke or fume event; erroneous delivery is assumed detected at donning and the crossover/second cylinder provides an alternate, giving a significant increase in workload to reconfigure and manage the degraded supply.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried, no occupant effect.
fha.judgementNote: SDD gives system function and redundancy (two cylinders, crossover, per-mask regulators) but does not substantiate detectability of erroneous delivery at the mask or its coincidence with an actual depressurisation. Assumed the error is detected at donning with a working alternate path (Major). Evidence that erroneous delivery could be undetected, or could coincide with a depressurisation with no alternate, would drive Hazardous (HAZ-2, crew unable to perform tasks).

assumptions.text: NZD open/close/latch and lock-sensing are aircraft functions, while the door's single-load-path structural and pressure-boundary integrity is structure, not a function.
assumptions.rationale: §5.7 mixes a mechanised behaviour (operate/latch/sense) with an explicit structural role; the modeling rule bars structure as a function, so I split them.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the safety organisation elects to carry door structural integrity functionally, an additional aircraft function would be added; otherwise it is handled by structural analysis and PRA.
assumptions.usedFor: Provide cargo access and pressure boundary at nose (all three sub-functions)

citations.quote: the door is a single load path and is treated as structure

assumptions.text: CRG blade restraint (straps, winches, tension monitoring) is a function, while the hold floor hard points that react restraint loads are structure.
assumptions.rationale: §5.8.3 states the hard points carry no redundancy and are structural; the mechanised restraint is a behaviour and is captured as a function.
assumptions.ifWrong: If hard-point integrity is to be tracked functionally rather than by structural analysis/PRA, an additional function or interface would be required.

citations.quote: There is no redundancy in the hold floor hard points

assumptions.text: The four resource systems (FUE, HYD, EPS, EWS) are not authored as aircraft functions; fuel delivery to engines is retained as a behaviour because the SDD states FUE 'delivers' and 'manages' rather than merely supplying a passive resource.
assumptions.rationale: §2.1 tags FUE/HYD/EPS/EWS as resources, but §5.2.1 describes FUE performing active delivery and mass-management behaviours; the modeling rule bars power/fuel as functions, creating a judgement boundary.
assumptions.ifWrong: If 'deliver fuel to engines' is judged a pure resource provision, that function and its two sub-functions are removed and captured only in the Resources model.

citations.quote: Four are treated as resources — they exist to supply other systems rather than to act on the aircraft

assumptions.text: Crew oxygen is authored as an aircraft function ('Provide crew oxygen') despite the SDD classifying OXY as a resource in the §2.1 inventory.
assumptions.rationale: §2.1 tags OXY 'Resource' but §5.13.1 describes a crew-protection behaviour the aircraft accomplishes; the resource/function boundary is ambiguous for a consumable that acts on the crew.
assumptions.ifWrong: If OXY is strictly a resource, the 'Provide crew oxygen' function and its sub-function are removed and the capability is captured only in the resources model.
assumptions.usedFor: Provide crew oxygen / Supply breathing oxygen to crew masks

citations.quote: OXY Crew Oxygen Resource Supplies flight crew; consumes ECS signal

assumptions.text: The nose cargo door is decomposed only as the open/close/lock behaviour (a function); its structural and pressure-boundary role is excluded from the functional decomposition.
assumptions.rationale: §5.7.3 states the door 'is treated as structure', and the modeling rule excludes structural support from functional-FHA items, but the same door also performs an operable behaviour.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the door's pressure-boundary integrity is to be treated functionally rather than structurally, an additional function would be required and the PRA/structural split changes.
assumptions.usedFor: Provide cargo access / Open, close and lock the nose cargo door

citations.quote: the door is a single load path and is treated as structure.

assumptions.text: Per-engine thrust is captured as one generic 'Generate propulsive thrust per engine' sub-function rather than four separately-failing rows.
assumptions.rationale: §5.1.5 shows left/right pairs in separate zones with non-commingled services, implying independence, but the SDD does not mandate four discrete function rows; granularity is a judgement.
assumptions.ifWrong: If per-engine independence must be modelled explicitly at function level, this single row splits into four independent sub-functions feeding the asymmetric-thrust directional-control case.
assumptions.usedFor: Provide thrust / Generate propulsive thrust per engine

citations.quote: Left and right engine pairs sit in separate zones.

assumptions.text: Fuel mass distribution error can develop below the 1,200 kg imbalance annunciation threshold, justifying a crew-Unaware malfunction variant for SF-004.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD gives the annunciation threshold but not the detection resolution below it, so an undetected sub-threshold drift is plausible and must carry its own Unaware row.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-004 Unaware row is removed and only the Aware malfunction row remains.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-004 Unaware row (Undetected fuel mass distribution error)

citations.quote: Fuel imbalance between left and right wings is annunciated at 1,200 kg and is limited structurally to 3,000 kg.

assumptions.text: An erroneous or slowly-diverging roll command/response can develop below crew detection thresholds when envelope protection and displays mask small deviations, justifying a crew-Unaware SF-005 malfunction row.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes annunciated degraded laws but does not establish detection thresholds for small erroneous roll behaviour, so an undetected variant cannot be dismissed for the whole function.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-005 Unaware row is removed and both roll malfunction variants remain only on the Aware row.

citations.quote: Degraded laws are annunciated.

assumptions.text: Reverse thrust is provided by the two inboard engines only, so its total loss and asymmetric partial loss are configuration facts feeding the SF-002 conditions.
assumptions.rationale: The reverser architecture governs which SF-002 partial/malfunction conditions are physically meaningful; the row wording assumes this two-inboard arrangement.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-002 asymmetric partial and inadvertent-deployment conditions would be re-scoped to the actual reverser count and placement.

citations.quote: Thrust reversers are fitted to the two inboard engines only.

assumptions.text: Erroneous or uncommanded pitch and yaw behaviour can develop below the crew's detection threshold, justifying a distinct crew-Unaware malfunction row for each axis.
assumptions.rationale: The function list and SDD give the actuation architecture but no detection-threshold data for the control axes, forcing a judgement on whether the unaware variant is applicable.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-006/SF-007 Unaware rows collapse into the Aware rows and the undetected malfunction conditions drop out of the matrix.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-006 Unaware row, SF-007 Unaware row

citations.quote: asymmetry and jam discretes

assumptions.text: Erroneous gear position indication can persist undetected because the two downlock circuits reporting agreement gives the crew no independent cue that the indication itself is wrong.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD grounds dual downlock sensing and flight-deck indication but does not state whether a failed indication is independently cross-checkable, forcing a judgement on the unaware case.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-010 Unaware row is removed and erroneous indication is captured only on the Aware row.

citations.quote: downlock status is sensed by two independent proximity circuits per unit

assumptions.text: Ground-load-support failures produce intrinsic, self-evident cues (attitude, ground contact) so no crew-Unaware variant is authored for SF-009.
assumptions.rationale: The function is a ground load-path behaviour with no annunciation described in the SDD; the awareness-dismissal reasoning is filed here per house style rather than in the matrix cell.
assumptions.ifWrong: An SF-009 Unaware row would be required for any degradation that can develop without a physical cue.

citations.quote: supports the aircraft on the ground, absorbs landing and taxi loads

assumptions.text: Ground deceleration and steering failures produce immediate heading/deceleration cues during the ground roll, so the crew-unaware variant is inapplicable except for a bias developing below the crew detection threshold.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD gives brake-temperature and steering command paths but no explicit alert for a small steering/braking bias, forcing a judgement on where the awareness split falls.
assumptions.ifWrong: If sub-threshold bias is not physically possible, the SF-012 Unaware row is deleted; if larger undetected losses are possible, the Unaware rows on SF-011/SF-012 must be broadened.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-012 Unaware row (Undetected erroneous ground steering); SF-011 awareness split

citations.quote: Brake temperature is monitored continuously and a turnaround limit is displayed.

assumptions.text: The nose visor is a ground-only function that cannot be operated in flight, so its failure conditions are confined to ground phases and the in-flight pressure-boundary hazard is carried by SF-014 lock integrity.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the door cannot be operated in flight, which determines whether SF-013 carries any in-flight condition or defers it to SF-014.
