praData.threat: Tire burst / flailing tread — main gear bogie (§25.734, AC 25.734-1)
praData.desc: Burst of a main-bogie tyre or thrown tread within a left/right main gear bay (Z710/Z720). Twenty tyres on six three-wheel bogies; gear-leg/bogie count is preliminary per SDD §1.2. Debris/tread is high-energy, radial and tangential, confined initially to the bay but able to sever or damage the adjacent brake hydraulic lines and, via the shared wing-root transit, the HYD A/B run in Z300.
praData.systems: LDG (brakes, wheel/tyre), HYD (systems A and B), FCS (surfaces on A/B supply)
praData.csfl: HYD A and B brake lines run through each main gear bay in adjacent, separately-clipped-and-shielded bundles sharing the bay (SDD §5.6.5) — a single burst in-bay is a common-cause candidate that can degrade both A and B braking; A and B also share a wing-root run (SDD §5.4.5), so bay debris reaching that transit threatens supplies to rudder/aileron/elevator actuation.
praData.mitigation:
Confirm bundle separation/shielding in the gear bay defeats a single tyre/tread trajectory taking both A and B; verify HYD A/B wing-root run is outside the credible tyre-debris cone; substantiate accumulator emergency braking (six applications, SDD §5.4.3) covers the degraded case. Outcome sought: SHOWN TO BE ACCEPTABLE via separation + accumulator reserve — to be substantiated.
Proposed requirements: • The LDG installation shall separate or shield the HYD A and B brake bundles in each main gear bay such that a single tyre burst or thrown tread cannot damage both.
• The HYD A/B wing-root run shall be located outside the credible tyre-debris trajectory from the main gear bays, or shielded against it.
aiRequirements: The LDG installation shall separate or shield the HYD A and B brake bundles in each main gear bay such that a single tyre burst or thrown tread cannot damage both.
The HYD A/B wing-root run shall be located outside the credible tyre-debris trajectory from the main gear bays, or shielded against it.

praData.threat: Bird strike — forward-facing structure, inlets and windshield (§25.571(e)(1)/§25.631/§33.76)
praData.desc: Bird impact on forward-facing surfaces: the four engine inlets (Z610–640), the flight-deck windshield (Z130), the wing leading edges (Z510/520) and the nose visor structure (Z110). Impact energy can ingest into an engine, crack a windshield, damage a leading edge and its anti-ice ducting, and strike the forward-fuselage-mounted probes and the two ice detectors.
praData.systems: PRP (inlets/ingestion), AVI (windshield, probes/air-data via forward-fuselage probes), IPS (leading-edge ducting, two same-type ice detectors), NZD (visor structure)
praData.csfl: The two ice detectors are of the same type, mounted on opposite sides of the forward fuselage (SDD §5.10.2) — a strike pattern is a common-mode candidate against ice detection; probes/static ports feeding the three ADIRUs are forward-fuselage-mounted and exposed. Ingestion into one engine is single-side; a flocking event challenging multiple inlets is the multi-engine scenario to be studied.
praData.mitigation:
Confirm windshield bird-strike capability per §25.631/§25.775; verify probe and ice-detector siting so a single strike cannot defeat air-data or ice-detection redundancy; substantiate engine ingestion tolerance per §33.76 against the inlet geometry. Outcome sought: SHOWN TO BE ACCEPTABLE (structure/windshield) and MINIMISED (multi-sensor loss via siting) — to be substantiated.
Proposed requirements: • The AVI/IPS installation shall site the air-data probes and the two ice detectors so that a single bird strike cannot simultaneously defeat air-data redundancy and ice-detection redundancy.
• The flight-deck windshield and forward structure shall withstand bird strike per the applicable §25.571(e)(1)/§25.631 threat without penetration endangering the crew.
aiRequirements: The AVI/IPS installation shall site the air-data probes and the two ice detectors so that a single bird strike cannot simultaneously defeat air-data redundancy and ice-detection redundancy.
The flight-deck windshield and forward structure shall withstand bird strike per the applicable §25.571(e)(1)/§25.631 threat without penetration endangering the crew.

praData.desc: Lightning attaches at aircraft extremities (nose visor, wing tips, engine nacelles, empennage) and conducts through the airframe. Survivability concern is coupling into the fly-by-wire FCS, avionics and electrical distribution carried on the six EWS routes; the two identified HV/LV crossing points in zone 300 and the wing-root region where the HV feeder co-transits with bleed ducts are the credible coupling points. Not a structural-integrity study (that is PRA/structural for the visor single load path); this row addresses the systems/electrical survivability.
praData.systems: FCS, AVI, EPS, EWS, PRP (FADEC), IPS
praData.csfl: A common electromagnetic transient could couple simultaneously into the three dissimilar flight control computers and the electrical distribution they depend on, defeating the FCS redundancy that is otherwise argued from three computers on three sources and three hydraulic systems.
praData.mitigation:
Bonding of metallic components and airframe per §25.581; nonmetallic/composite lightning protection design; transient protection and shielding of the EWS routes; separation of HV and LV routes maintained except at the two shielded crossing points; standby instrument on the DC essential bus wired on an independent route. Outcome claimed: effects SHOWN ACCEPTABLE via §25.1316 qualification — pending test/analysis.
Proposed requirements: • The aircraft structure and metallic components shall be bonded to the airframe to protect against catastrophic effects of lightning (§25.581).
• The electrical and electronic systems performing functions whose failure would be Catastrophic or Hazardous shall be protected against the effects of lightning to §25.1316 levels.
• The EWS HV/LV route separation and the two shielded crossing points shall be shown to preserve FCS/AVI independence under a lightning transient.
aiFunctions: SF-023 Provide flight and navigation display
SF-024 Provide air data and inertial reference
aiRequirements: The aircraft structure and metallic components shall be bonded to the airframe to protect against catastrophic effects of lightning (§25.581).
The electrical and electronic systems performing functions whose failure would be Catastrophic or Hazardous shall be protected against the effects of lightning to §25.1316 levels.
The EWS HV/LV route separation and the two shielded crossing points shall be shown to preserve FCS/AVI independence under a lightning transient.

praData.desc: External radiated fields couple into the low-voltage signal routes, the two data network channels and the electronic units (FCC, ADIRU, display processors) distributed along the fuselage. Survivability concern is erroneous or misleading data reaching the control laws and displays rather than structural effect; the two HV/LV crossing points in zone 300 and the data-network routing (zones 120,200,300,400,800) are the credible coupling paths.
praData.csfl: A radiated field is by nature a common-mode threat that can couple simultaneously into otherwise-independent LV/data routes and the three flight control computers and three reference units, so the independence argued from routing on opposite sides must be shown to hold under illumination.
praData.mitigation:
HIRF protection design and equipment qualification to §25.1317; shielding and bundle segregation of the LV and data routes; opposite-side routing of the two data network channels sharing no connector or penetration; the standby integrated instrument sharing no supply, sensor or processing with the primary displays as an independent means. Outcome claimed: effects SHOWN ACCEPTABLE via §25.1317 qualification — pending test/analysis.
Proposed requirements: • Each electrical and electronic system that performs a function whose failure would be Catastrophic or Hazardous shall be designed and installed to be unaffected by HIRF to §25.1317 levels.
• The two data network channels and the LV signal routes shall be shown to preserve avionics independence under HIRF illumination.
• The standby integrated instrument independence (no shared supply, sensor or processing) shall be substantiated under a HIRF environment.
aiFunctions: SF-023 Provide flight and navigation display
SF-024 Provide air data and inertial reference
aiRequirements: Each electrical and electronic system that performs a function whose failure would be Catastrophic or Hazardous shall be designed and installed to be unaffected by HIRF to §25.1317 levels.
The two data network channels and the LV signal routes shall be shown to preserve avionics independence under HIRF illumination.
The standby integrated instrument independence (no shared supply, sensor or processing) shall be substantiated under a HIRF environment.

praData.threat: Hail / ice impact on forward-facing structure, inlets and probes
praData.desc: App L survivability study of hail/ice impact per §25.571(e)(2) on forward-facing surfaces. Model: hail/ice mass striking wing/stabiliser leading edges, the four engine inlet cowls, windshields and the pitot/static/AoA probes and the two forward-fuselage ice detectors. Drawing/model-stage installation per SDD — routing and detector positions are described, not frozen; treat trajectory/geometry as preliminary. Direct in-zone strike on leading edges (510/520) and engine inlets (nacelles 610-640); windshield and probe strike at the forward fuselage/flight deck (120/130).
praData.csfl: Ice detectors are of the same type installed on opposite sides of the forward fuselage (SDD §5.10.2/§5.10.3) — a single hail/ice-impact environment strikes both, a common-source loss of both detection channels defeating the assumed detector redundancy for ice accretion detection. Probe/windshield heating and the primary air-data path can be degraded concurrently with the standby path where both face the impact environment; independence of the standby instrument from the airstream sensing is not established for a common environmental impact.
praData.mitigation:
Existing design features: probes, static ports, windshields and both ice detectors are electrically heated and individually monitored (§5.10.2); wing leading edges and inlet cowls have bleed anti-ice available from either side via the cross-bleed manifold (§5.10.3); wing anti-ice ducting shares the leading edge with the outboard electrical route behind a shielded partition (§5.10.5). CLAIM: effects on ice-protection availability are MINIMISED by heated-element monitoring and cross-bleed redundancy; the two-same-type ice-detector common-source loss must be SHOWN ACCEPTABLE. Impact-resistance of windshields, leading edges and inlets is a structural showing under §25.571(e)(2) not settled here.
Proposed requirements: • The forward-facing structure, engine inlets and windshields shall withstand the hail/ice impact threat of the certification basis without loss of a Catastrophic or Hazardous function.
• The two ice detectors shall be shown to retain ice-accretion detection following a single hail/ice-impact environment, or the common-source loss shall be substantiated as acceptable.
aiRequirements: The forward-facing structure, engine inlets and windshields shall withstand the hail/ice impact threat of the certification basis without loss of a Catastrophic or Hazardous function.
The two ice detectors shall be shown to retain ice-accretion detection following a single hail/ice-impact environment, or the common-source loss shall be substantiated as acceptable.

praData.threat: Icing / ice accretion and ice shedding
praData.desc: App L survivability study of in-flight icing per §25.1419 / AC 20-73A within the type-design ice envelope. Model: ice accretion on unprotected or under-protected surfaces, inlets, probes and detectors; and ice shed from wing/stabiliser leading edges, inlet cowls and the fuselage into the engine inlets and onto aft structure. Direct in-zone effect on wing/stabiliser leading edges (510/520/800), engine inlets (610-640) and forward-fuselage probes/windshields/detectors (120/130). Drawing/model-stage installation — ice-envelope refinement and detector positions per SDD are preliminary.
praData.csfl: Wing and inlet anti-ice both draw hot bleed from the SAME cross-bleed manifold that supplies the ECS packs (§5.10.2) — loss or contention of that manifold is a common source degrading wing anti-ice, cowl anti-ice and pack conditioning together. Both same-type ice detectors accrete in the same icing environment, defeating detection redundancy (§5.10.3). Shed ice from a leading edge/cowl can enter one or more of the four inlets, a single environmental event reaching multiple otherwise-independent engines.
praData.mitigation:
Existing design features: bleed protection to wings and cowls available from either side via the cross-bleed manifold; six independently supplied electrically-heated stabiliser zones with a lost zone annunciated; individually monitored heated probes/ports/windshields; ice detection advisory with automatic activation and manual selection (§5.10.2/§5.10.3). CLAIM: effects on continued safe flight in icing are MINIMISED by dual-side bleed, independent stabiliser zones and monitored probe heat; the shared cross-bleed-manifold common source and the two-same-type detector common-source loss must be SHOWN ACCEPTABLE; engine ingestion of shed ice is an engine/installation showing (§33.76/§25.1093) not settled here.
Proposed requirements: • The ice protection system shall provide continued safe flight and landing within the certification-basis icing envelope with any single anti-ice bleed source or manifold segment lost.
• Ice shed from protected and unprotected surfaces shall be shown not to cause a Hazardous or Catastrophic effect on the engine installation or aft structure.
• The two same-type ice detectors shall be shown to retain ice-accretion detection in the design icing environment, or the common-source loss shall be substantiated as acceptable.
aiRequirements: The ice protection system shall provide continued safe flight and landing within the certification-basis icing envelope with any single anti-ice bleed source or manifold segment lost.
Ice shed from protected and unprotected surfaces shall be shown not to cause a Hazardous or Catastrophic effect on the engine installation or aft structure.
The two same-type ice detectors shall be shown to retain ice-accretion detection in the design icing environment, or the common-source loss shall be substantiated as acceptable.

praData.desc: Fire or smoke originating in the pressurised hold (zones 200/300/400) or the forward equipment bay/flight deck (120/130). Hold carries smoke detection at nine stations along its length with NO suppression fitted (SDD §5.12.2) — a deliberate design decision recorded as an assumption to be substantiated. Zone 120 houses oxygen cylinders and forward avionics racks; zone 130 is the occupied flight deck with fire handles and crew oxygen masks. Cross-zone propagation reaches otherwise-separated equipment along shared runs: the HV feeder (610/620,530,300,200), LV signal (120,200,300,400,800), data channels (120,200,300,400,800) and the restraint tension monitoring loop (200,300,400), all of which transit the hold zones. A hold fire beneath the blade near an FCC bay (FCC 2 in zone 300, FCC 3 in zone 400) or the HV/LV crossing points in zone 300 could defeat the three-computer / dual-network independence claim by common-cause thermal damage.
praData.systems: FPR (detection zones 200/300/400, no hold suppression), CRG (restraint tension loop + winches in hold), AVI (FCC 2 zone 300, FCC 3 zone 400, network channels), EPS (HV feeder transit), OXY (cylinders zone 120), FCS (via FCC common-mode), ECS (conditioning/smoke evacuation of hold and flight deck)
praData.csfl: A hold fire in zone 300 concurrently threatens FCC 2, the HV/LV crossing points and the data network, and via routing reaches FCC 3 (zone 400) and the HV feeder to zone 200 — a single localised thermal event as common cause across the flight-control computer, electrical feeder and data-network independence claimed in SDD §5.3.5 and §5.11.5.
praData.mitigation:
Detection: dual-loop continuous detection in nacelle/APU zones, nine-station smoke detection along the hold (SDD §5.12.2). Segregation: HV and LV routes separated throughout except two shielded crossing points in zone 300; data channels on opposite sides sharing no connector/penetration; three FCCs in three separate bays. Crew: fire handles and portable extinguishers at flight deck and hold access door; crew oxygen with smoke goggles. GAP — NO hold suppression is fitted; acceptability of detection-only rests on the single-blade / no-combustible-palletised-load argument and MUST be substantiated. Consequence for the crossing points, FCC bays and HV/LV co-location in zone 300 is not yet shown ELIMINATED, MINIMISED or ACCEPTABLE.
Proposed requirements: • The FPR system shall provide the means to detect fire/smoke throughout the hold at a coverage and response time consistent with the no-suppression decision, and the acceptability of detection-only shall be substantiated by analysis of hold fire load and propagation (SDD §5.12.2 open assumption).
• The installation shall demonstrate that a single hold fire in zone 300 cannot simultaneously defeat the independence of FCC 2, the HV/LV crossing points and the data network channels claimed for flight-control and display functions (thermal separation/shielding at the zone-300 crossing points).
aiRequirements: The FPR system shall provide the means to detect fire/smoke throughout the hold at a coverage and response time consistent with the no-suppression decision, and the acceptability of detection-only shall be substantiated by analysis of hold fire load and propagation (SDD §5.12.2 open assumption).

The installation shall demonstrate that a single hold fire in zone 300 cannot simultaneously defeat the independence of FCC 2, the HV/LV crossing points and the data network channels claimed for flight-control and display functions (thermal separation/shielding at the zone-300 crossing points).

zsaData.desc: Nose visor structure — pressure boundary when closed, unpressurised when open. Houses visor latches, lock pins, lock actuator, sensing harness (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Twelve rotary latches on common torque shaft, eight locking pins, lock actuator, proximity sensing harness
zsaData.interference: Single load-path door structure with no structural redundancy; lock sensing harness transits 110→120→130 and must stay separated from door actuation power and from the mechanical indicator linkage. Installation/maintenance error could commingle the two dissimilar sensing paths or the sensing harness with actuation power, defeating the dual-dissimilar sensing claim.
zsaData.mitigation: Verify sensing harness routed opposite door actuation power and separated from mechanical indicator linkage throughout, with the two bulkhead penetrations at the flight-deck bulkhead separated (SDD §5.7.5); confirm pressure interlock wiring integrity. Door structural integrity substantiated by structural analysis / PRA, not by ZSA.

zsaData.desc: Forward equipment bay — pressurised, conditioned. Houses FCC 1, oxygen cylinders, forward avionics racks (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Flight control computer 1, high-pressure oxygen cylinders, forward avionics racks; LV signal and data channel routes originate/transit here
zsaData.interference: Co-location of high-pressure oxygen cylinders with FCC 1 and avionics racks; an oxygen cylinder overpressure/leak or a maintenance handling error near energised avionics is an inherent physical hazard assessed regardless of functional criticality (App K.3.1). LV signal left/right and data channels 1/2 transit this zone.
zsaData.mitigation: Confirm cylinders installed outside any high-energy electrical source zone per SDD §5.13.5 and thermal discharge routed overboard; verify FCC 1 separation from the other two FCCs (mid/aft bays) is preserved so the three-computer dissimilarity is not defeated by common installation in this bay. Bonding/segregation of oxygen supply line clear of feeders.

zsaData.desc: Flight deck — pressurised, occupied. Houses displays, inceptors, standby instrument, fire handles, crew oxygen masks (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Four display units, inceptors, integrated standby instrument, fire handles, crew oxygen masks
zsaData.interference: Occupied compartment; standby instrument must share no supply/sensor/processing with primary displays (SDD §5.11.3) — an installation error commingling the standby feeder with primary display feeders defeats the independence claim. Lock-status indication and fire-handle runs terminate here.
zsaData.mitigation: Verify standby instrument wired directly to DC essential bus on a route independent of primary display feeders (SDD §5.11.5); confirm crew-oxygen mask stowage and quick-don access unobstructed. Housekeeping/materials-compatibility checkpoint for an occupied zone.

zsaData.desc: Forward hold (stations 1–3) — low differential, unoccupied. Houses saddles 1–3, restraint straps, tension loop, smoke detectors (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Saddles 1–3 with two tension straps each, single instrumented restraint tension loop, smoke detectors; HV feeder, LV signal, data channels, HYD C run and fuel gallery vent transit
zsaData.interference: The single instrumented restraint tension monitoring loop runs full hold length on the left side and shares this zone with the fuel gallery vent and the left-side electrical route (SDD §5.8.5) — a single event in the shared zone could disable restraint monitoring and expose an electrical/fuel-vapour co-location. HV feeder and HYD C also transit.
zsaData.mitigation: Confirm the single tension loop separation from the fuel gallery vent and left electrical route; verify smoke-detector coverage at the station; confirm HV feeder / HYD C separation maintained through the zone. Co-location of the single-loop monitor is a recorded item (SDD §5.8.5).

zsaData.desc: Mid hold (stations 4–6) — low differential, unoccupied. Houses saddles 4–6, mid equipment bay, FCC 2, HV/LV crossing points (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Saddles 4–6, mid equipment bay, FCC 2; HYD A+B shared wing-root run, HYD C, HV feeder L/R, LV signal, data channels, bleed cross-bleed manifold, restraint loop all transit
zsaData.interference: This zone concentrates several nominally independent items: the two HV↔LV crossing points (SDD §5.5.5/§5.14.2), the HYD A+B shared wing-root run (SDD §5.4.5), the cross-bleed manifold joining both sides (SDD §5.9.5), and FCC 2. A single installation/maintenance event here could defeat multiple independence claims at once — the primary common-mode candidate zone.
zsaData.mitigation: Verify HV/LV crossing points use the defined shielding and minimum distance; confirm HYD A and B bundles separately clipped where they share the run; confirm FCC 2 separation from FCC 1/3 preserved. Reflect the A+B shared run and HV/LV crossings as common-cause contributors in the affected fault trees (ARP4761A particular-risk/zonal complement).

zsaData.desc: Aft hold (stations 7–9) — low differential, unoccupied. Houses saddles 7–9, aft equipment bay, FCC 3 (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Saddles 7–9, aft equipment bay, FCC 3; HYD C run, LV signal, data channels and restraint loop transit
zsaData.interference: FCC 3 co-located with restraint saddles and HYD C run; the third of three dissimilar computers must remain separated from FCC 1 (120) and FCC 2 (300) for the dissimilarity argument to hold. Restraint tension loop continues through this zone.
zsaData.mitigation: Confirm FCC 3 bay separation preserves the three-bay computer distribution (SDD §5.3.5); verify HYD C run and restraint loop separation maintained; smoke-detection coverage at aft stations.

zsaData.desc: Left wing box and leading edge — flammable fluid present. Houses fuel tanks, cross-feed gallery, wing anti-ice ducting, outboard electrical route (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Integral fuel tanks, cross-feed gallery, wing anti-ice ducting, outboard electrical route
zsaData.interference: Flammable-fluid zone with a hot bleed anti-ice duct and an electrical route sharing the leading edge behind a shielded partition (SDD §5.10.5). Installation error or partition degradation co-locates an ignition source with fuel vapour. The single spanwise cross-feed gallery — the only path from one wing to the opposite engines — transits here.
zsaData.mitigation: Verify the shielded partition integrity between anti-ice ducting and the outboard electrical route along the full run; confirm tank vent/surge lines routed outboard of all electrical harnesses (SDD §5.2.5); drainage and ventilation of the flammable zone. Cross-feed gallery retained for particular-risk/zonal attention.

zsaData.desc: Right wing box and leading edge — flammable fluid present. Mirror of 510: fuel tanks, cross-feed gallery, wing anti-ice ducting, outboard electrical route (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Integral fuel tanks, cross-feed gallery, wing anti-ice ducting, outboard electrical route; single pressure refuel/defuel point at right wing root
zsaData.interference: Flammable-fluid zone as 510 (mirrored). Additionally the single pressure refuel/defuel point is in the right wing root (SDD §5.2.2) — a refuelling/servicing error is a maintenance-error checkpoint. Hot anti-ice duct shares the leading edge with the outboard electrical route behind a shielded partition.
zsaData.mitigation: Verify shielded partition integrity; confirm overflow protection circuit independence at the refuel point (SDD §5.2.2); tank vent lines outboard of electrical harnesses; drainage/ventilation of the flammable zone.

zsaData.desc: Left wing root — pressure boundary transit. Houses HYD A and B wing-root run, bleed duct penetration, HV feeder transit (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: HYD A and B wing-root run (shared), bleed duct penetration, HV feeder transit
zsaData.interference: HYD systems A and B share this wing-root run where both cross the pressure boundary (SDD §5.4.5) — a claim about independence the SDD itself flags for a dedicated zonal item. A single event at this run could take both A and B, degrading flight controls, gear and braking simultaneously. HV feeder and bleed duct penetrate the same boundary region.
zsaData.mitigation: Confirm A and B are on separate routes to the maximum extent and separately clipped where they share the run; verify bleed duct kept clear of the HV feeder with the minimum separation (SDD §5.9.5). Reflect the A+B shared run as a common-cause contributor in the FCS/LDG fault trees.

zsaData.desc: Right wing root — pressure boundary transit. Mirror of 530: HYD A and B wing-root run, bleed duct penetration, HV feeder transit (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: HYD A and B wing-root run (shared), bleed duct penetration, HV feeder transit
zsaData.interference: As 530 (mirrored): HYD A and B share the wing-root run crossing the pressure boundary; bleed duct and HV feeder transit the same region. Single-event common-cause candidate for both A and B.
zsaData.mitigation: As 530 — confirm A/B separate clipping, bleed-duct/HV separation, and reflect the shared run as a common-cause contributor in the affected fault trees.

zsaData.desc: Engine nacelle 2 — high energy, flammable fluid, fire zone (§25.1181). Engine, FADEC, generator, EDP, fire detection loops, extinguisher plumbing (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Engine 2, dual-channel FADEC, 150 kVA generator, engine-driven hydraulic pump (HYD A), dual fire-detection loops, extinguisher plumbing
zsaData.interference: Designated fire zone per §25.1181 as 610. Rotor/engine burst are cross-zone PRA-owned hazards. Dual-loop detection separation and cross-bottle plumbing to nacelle 1 must be preserved.
zsaData.mitigation: As 610 — verify loop separation, fire-zone drainage/ventilation, and cross-plumbing to the paired nacelle. Cross-reference rotor-burst/engine-burst PRA.

zsaData.desc: Engine nacelle 3 — high energy, flammable fluid, fire zone (§25.1181). Engine, FADEC, generator, EDP, fire detection loops, extinguisher plumbing (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Engine 3, dual-channel FADEC, 150 kVA generator, engine-driven hydraulic pump (HYD B), dual fire-detection loops, extinguisher plumbing
zsaData.interference: Designated fire zone per §25.1181. Nacelle 3 drives HYD B; rotor/engine burst are cross-zone PRA-owned. Dual-loop detection separation and cross-bottle plumbing to nacelle 4 must be preserved.
zsaData.mitigation: As 610/620 — verify loop separation, fire-zone drainage/ventilation, cross-plumbing to nacelle 4; cross-reference rotor-burst/engine-burst PRA.

zsaData.desc: Engine nacelle 4 — high energy, flammable fluid, fire zone (§25.1181). Engine, FADEC, generator, EDP, fire detection loops, extinguisher plumbing (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Engine 4, dual-channel FADEC, 150 kVA generator, engine-driven hydraulic pump (HYD B), dual fire-detection loops, extinguisher plumbing
zsaData.interference: Designated fire zone per §25.1181. Outboard engine 4 is the sizing case for asymmetric-thrust directional control (SDD §5.1.3); rotor/engine burst are cross-zone PRA-owned. Detection separation and cross-plumbing to nacelle 3 must be preserved.
zsaData.mitigation: As the other nacelles — verify loop separation, fire-zone drainage/ventilation, cross-plumbing to nacelle 3; cross-reference rotor-burst/engine-burst PRA.

zsaData.desc: Left main gear bay — unpressurised, overheat detection fitted. Houses three bogies, brake lines A and B, steering and brake harnesses (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Three three-wheel bogies, brake hydraulic lines A and B, steering and brake electrical harnesses, overheat detection
zsaData.interference: Brake hydraulic lines for systems A and B run through the bay in adjacent (separately clipped) bundles, sharing the zone (SDD §5.6.5) — a single bay event (tyre burst / flailing tread, brake overheat) could affect both supplies. Tyre burst is an APPLICABLE cross-zone particular risk (PRA-81342). Steering and brake harnesses on opposite sides.
zsaData.mitigation: Verify A/B brake bundles separately clipped and shielded per SDD §5.6.5; confirm overheat detection coverage; confirm steering vs brake harness separation. Tyre-burst/flailing-tread debris addressed by PRA-81342 (co-located), reflected as common-cause where it defeats A/B independence.

zsaData.desc: Right main gear bay — unpressurised, overheat detection fitted. Mirror of 710: three bogies, brake lines A and B, steering and brake harnesses (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Three three-wheel bogies, brake hydraulic lines A and B, steering and brake electrical harnesses, overheat detection
zsaData.interference: As 710 (mirrored): brake lines A and B share the bay; tyre burst is an APPLICABLE cross-zone particular risk (PRA-81342); brake overheat detection fitted.
zsaData.mitigation: As 710 — verify A/B brake bundle separation, overheat coverage, harness separation; cross-reference tyre-burst PRA-81342.

zsaData.desc: Nose gear bay — unpressurised. Houses nose unit, steering actuator, tow disconnect (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Twin-wheel steerable nose unit, hydraulic steering actuator, tow disconnect (mechanical)
zsaData.interference: Steerable nose unit with a mechanical tow disconnect — a maintenance/towing error (disconnect not re-engaged, steering mis-rigged) is a maintenance-error checkpoint. Tyre burst on the nose unit is a co-located APPLICABLE particular risk (PRA-81342).
zsaData.mitigation: Verify tow-disconnect re-engagement is a positive, indicated action per operating procedure; confirm steering actuator supply integrity; drainage of the unpressurised bay. Cross-reference tyre-burst PRA-81342.

zsaData.desc: Aft fuselage and empennage — mixed; APU is a fire zone (§25.1181). Houses rudder control runs, stabiliser heater feeders, APU compartment (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Rudder upper/lower control runs, stabiliser heater feeders (six zones), APU compartment with dedicated fire bottle
zsaData.interference: Mixed-environment zone flagged as a candidate for sub-partitioning per App K.4.1: it contains a designated fire zone (APU per §25.1181) alongside rudder control runs and stabiliser heater feeders. Rudder upper/lower segments and their control runs are on opposite sides of the aft fuselage; stabiliser heater feeders must stay opposite the rudder runs (SDD §5.10.5). An APU fire or a heater-feeder fault must not take both rudder segment runs.
zsaData.mitigation: Recommend sub-partitioning the APU fire zone from the control-run bay for a uniform environment (App K.4.1); verify rudder upper/lower runs on opposite sides and stabiliser heater feeders opposite the rudder runs; confirm APU auto-discharge and fuel-isolation on the ground unattended (SDD §5.12.2), and APU-zone drainage/ventilation.

zsaData.desc: Engine nacelle 1 — high energy, flammable fluid, fire zone (§25.1181). Houses engine, FADEC, generator, EDP, fire detection loops, extinguisher plumbing (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Engine 1, dual-channel FADEC, 150 kVA generator, engine-driven hydraulic pump (HYD A), dual fire-detection loops, extinguisher plumbing
zsaData.interference: Designated fire zone per §25.1181 with flammable fluid and high-energy rotating machinery. Inherent physical hazards — uncontained rotor burst and high-energy engine burst — extend beyond the zone and are PRA-owned (App K.3.1). Dual detection loops must be routed on opposite sides of the zone for the AND logic to survive a single event.
zsaData.mitigation: Verify the two detection loops routed separately/opposite sides and separately clipped (SDD §5.12.5); confirm drainage and ventilation of the fire zone (§29.1187 analogue for transport per §25.1181); confirm extinguisher cross-plumbing to the paired nacelle. Rotor/engine burst debris addressed by PRA-81342-class rotor-burst/engine-burst analysis, not this ZSA row.

taskRows.task: Isolate a failed engine by closing the associated fuel shut-off and fire handle
Control thrust through four thrust levers with autothrottle
Select manual cross-feed and isolate any fuel tank
Select the hydraulic electric pumps on or off and command the power transfer unit
Manually override ram air turbine deployment
Operate landing gear by gear lever and apply braking by brake pedals, with autobrake available
Perform alternate landing gear extension from the separate handle
Operate the nose cargo door from the ground handling panel with the aircraft on jacks or gear
Verify nose door lock status as part of the take-off configuration check
Select environmental control pack configuration and bleed source
Select ice protection automatic or manual operation
Interact with the displays, flight management computers and alerting list; select reversionary display
Command engine or APU extinguishing through the fire handles
Don crew oxygen mask on crew action
Perform the pre-flight crew oxygen pressure check

cdRows.supports: Identifying non-normal system conditions and the appropriate crew action across every aircraft system
cdRows.finding: The alerting system consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list with associated procedures, driven by two independent processing channels.

cdRows.item: Consolidated prioritised crew alert list — prioritisation hierarchy
cdRows.supports: Detecting and responding to multiple simultaneous alerts in order of urgency
cdRows.finding: The list is described as prioritised but the document does not state the warning/caution/advisory hierarchy, attention-getting cues, or that cues span two senses; alerting means against §25.1322(b)/(c) are [not stated].

cdRows.supports: Crew awareness of reduced roll and pitch control authority following flight control computer or hydraulic degradation
cdRows.finding: Degraded laws are annunciated; reversion to mechanical control is not a selectable mode and results from loss of all electrical command paths.

cdRows.supports: Commanding roll and pitch with envelope protection active in the normal control law
cdRows.finding: The crew flies through conventional inceptors with envelope protection active in the normal control law; degraded laws are annunciated.

cdRows.item: Flight control asymmetry and jam discretes
cdRows.supports: Detecting surface asymmetry or jam affecting roll and pitch control
cdRows.finding: The flight control system outputs surface position, system status, flight envelope protection status, and asymmetry and jam discretes to the avionics displays.

cdRows.supports: Normal thrust control and isolation of a failed engine
cdRows.finding: Normal control is by four thrust levers with autothrottle; the only crew action to isolate a failed engine is to close the associated fuel shut-off and fire handle.

cdRows.supports: Monitoring engine state for detecting loss of forward thrust and uncommanded thrust change
cdRows.finding: Engine parameter data is output to the avionics display system; the FADEC protects against overspeed and overtemperature without crew intervention.

cdRows.supports: Preventing inadvertent or uncommanded reverse thrust in flight
cdRows.finding: Reverser deployment is inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement, with a mechanical lock at the translating sleeve.

cdRows.supports: Detecting loss of fuel delivery pressure and lateral fuel imbalance
cdRows.finding: Low-pressure and imbalance discretes are output to the flight deck; fuel imbalance is annunciated at 1,200 kg and limited structurally to 3,000 kg.

cdRows.item: Manual cross-feed and tank isolation selection
cdRows.supports: Intervening in fuel mass management and delivery when automatic scheduling is inadequate
cdRows.finding: The system is normally automatic; the crew can select manual cross-feed and can isolate any tank.

cdRows.supports: Monitoring fuel mass distribution to detect distribution error
cdRows.finding: Tank quantity and temperature are output to the avionics; the document does not state a means to detect an undetected fuel mass distribution error.

cdRows.supports: Recovering flight, navigation and system information following display or processor loss
cdRows.finding: Any display unit can present any format; reversionary display selection is manual and network reconfiguration is automatic.

cdRows.supports: Providing attitude, airspeed and altitude for pitch and roll control after loss of primary displays
cdRows.finding: Standby attitude, airspeed and altitude are provided by an independent integrated standby instrument on the DC essential bus that shares no supply, no sensor and no processing with the primary displays.

saRows.element: Loss of a source (generator/bus) — bus reconfiguration is otherwise automatic and silent
saRows.cue: Source-loss annunciation on the crew alerting list; battery-only remaining endurance displayed

saRows.element: Wing fuel imbalance between left and right wings
saRows.cue: Imbalance annunciated at 1,200 kg; imbalance discrete to the flight deck

saRows.element: Erroneous or undetected fuel mass distribution given normally automatic transfer/cross-feed
saRows.finding: Transfer and cross-feed are scheduled automatically without crew action; documents describe imbalance annunciation and low-pressure discretes but no cue specific to an undetected distribution error is described

saRows.element: Engine fuel low-pressure condition (partial/complete loss of fuel delivery)
saRows.cue: Low-pressure discretes to the flight deck

saRows.element: Degraded flight control law following loss of command paths
saRows.cue: Degraded laws are annunciated; flight envelope protection status to the avionics displays

saRows.element: Surface asymmetry or jam affecting roll/pitch control authority
saRows.cue: Asymmetry and jam discretes; surface position and system status to the avionics displays

saRows.element: Reversion to mechanical control (all three flight control computers lost)
saRows.finding: Reversion to mechanical control is not a selectable mode and results from loss of all electrical command paths; documents describe degraded-law annunciation but do not describe a dedicated cue for the reversion state itself

saRows.element: Uncommanded reverse thrust in flight — reverser deployment is inhibited by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement
saRows.finding: Documents describe the in-flight deployment inhibit and mechanical translating-sleeve lock but do not describe a flight-deck cue that annunciates an uncommanded reverse thrust condition

saRows.element: Thrust levels and engine parameters across four engines (symmetric/asymmetric thrust loss)
saRows.cue: Engine parameter data to the avionics display system; fire and overheat discretes to the flight deck

hfaRows.text: Complete loss of forward thrust means simultaneous loss of all four engines and is not recoverable by crew action, driving Catastrophic.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The credited symmetric and single-engine asymmetric partial-loss cases are recoverable within the one-engine-inoperative dispatch design case with rudder authority sized to the outboard failure.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Uncommanded and erroneous thrust cases are credited at the recoverable-excursion outcome (crew arrests the asymmetry), not an unrecoverable loss of directional control, because FADEC protects overspeed/overtemperature and the failure is not assumed simultaneous across all engines.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Wheel braking and spoilers hold the aircraft within the 1,800 m landing distance requirement with reverse thrust lost on a semi-prepared surface.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The FCS directional-control sizing leaves recoverable rudder/roll authority against an inboard-engine uncommanded in-flight reverse asymmetry.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Inadvertent reverser deployment on the ground is recoverable via rejected takeoff or steering within available runway.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Loss or partial loss of fuel delivery to a single engine is bounded by the design's continue-to-a-suitable-aerodrome capability after loss of any one engine.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The crew act on the 1,200 kg imbalance annunciation and use manual cross-feed to keep imbalance within the 3,000 kg structural limit and CG within limits.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Cross-feed reconfiguration is available to restore balanced delivery for an asymmetric partial fuel-delivery loss.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Erroneous or uncommanded fuel distribution, once annunciated at 1,200 kg, can be arrested by crew manual cross-feed/tank isolation before reaching the 3,000 kg structural imbalance limit.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Exceeding the 3,000 kg lateral imbalance limit undetected produces a large reduction in safety margins (structural/CG consequence) rather than an immediate catastrophic outcome.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: A partial loss of roll control leaves at least one hydraulic supply feeding the ailerons and spoilers, retaining roll authority sufficient to control the aircraft with increased crew workload.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: An erroneous or uncommanded roll near the ground is not recoverable by crew action and is credited as driving hull loss.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: In the undetected roll conditions the erroneous or uncommanded roll is not annunciated, so the crew do not act until the excursion is developed and unrecoverable.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The mechanical reversion path to stabiliser trim provides a survivable but degraded means of pitch control adequate for continued safe flight and landing.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: A within-MAC partial loss of pitch control leaves the aircraft controllable with increased workload and no loss of continued safe flight.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: An erroneous or uncommanded pitch input can develop into an attitude excursion outside the recoverable flight envelope before crew action arrests it.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: An erroneous pitch response can occur with no annunciation and no crew cue, leaving the crew unaware and uncorrecting.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: An undetected uncommanded pitch motion is unbounded and diverges to loss of control if the crew takes no action.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The outboard-engine 28 m moment arm at V1 with maximum blade payload is the sizing directional-control case, so yaw-authority sufficiency is judged against countering that asymmetric thrust.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: An erroneous yaw response is detectable by the crew through heading/sideslip cues and arrestable, keeping it recoverable rather than an unrecoverable departure.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Directional control is sized by an outboard-engine-out case at the 28 m moment arm, so uncommanded/erroneous yaw excursions are most critical at low speed near the ground and rate as a large safety-margin reduction.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: An undetected erroneous/uncommanded yaw condition means no annunciation is credited and crew recognition cannot be used as an alleviating factor.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: With high-lift lost or reduced, the aircraft can still be landed at higher speed within a workable field margin, so complete and partial loss are Major rather than Hazardous.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight, so the occupant axis for all rows is limited to the flight crew.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The high-lift asymmetry brakes arrest a differential deployment to a rolling moment the crew can control with available roll authority at low speed.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Loss of high-lift asymmetry annunciation delays crew corrective action beyond the point where aerodynamic cues alone give timely warning near the ground.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Complete loss of ground load support results in structural collapse of the loaded airframe not arrestable by crew action.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Partial loss of ground support (a bogie or leg) cannot be fully carried by the remaining units on the semi-prepared surface where flotation margin is the sizing case.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: A gear-up landing of the HL-1 on the 1,800 m semi-prepared strip is survivable (crew only) but not routinely so, supporting Hazardous rather than Catastrophic.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Both normal (HYD A) and the free-fall alternate extension can be jointly lost for the complete-loss condition to occur.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: No weight-on-wheels ground-retraction inhibit precludes an uncommanded gear retraction during takeoff/landing ground phases.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: A false down-and-locked indication can persist undetected despite the two dissimilar, independently routed downlock sensing paths.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Complete loss of ground deceleration on the 1,800 m semi-prepared strip cannot be arrested by reverse thrust and aerodynamic drag alone, producing an unrecoverable overrun.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Directional control authority is insufficient to fully arrest an asymmetric-braking yaw excursion at high ground speed on the low-friction semi-prepared surface, but the excursion stops short of hull loss.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Uncommanded and erroneous ground deceleration are symmetric (both sides) and bounded such that the crew can detect and compensate within the available stopping distance.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight so there are no passengers to injure in any of these conditions.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Ground steering acts only in ground phases (taxi, take-off roll, landing roll) and is weight-on-wheels gated, so no in-flight effect exists.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Differential braking and rudder provide adequate alternate directional control on the ground when steering is lost or degraded, capping the annunciated loss/malfunction cases at Major.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The landing/take-off surface is a 1,800 m semi-prepared strip with ~1,080 m predicted rollout, so lateral runway margin for a directional excursion is limited.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Loss, partial loss, uncommanded and inadvertent nose visor OPERATION cannot affect an already-closed, locked door in flight because the door cannot be operated in flight.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The nose door, when closed, is a primary pressure-boundary and forward-fuselage structural load-path element whose in-flight failure to remain secured leads to door opening/separation.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight and the aircraft carries flight crew only, so there are no passengers to injure in any nose-door failure condition.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Loss of a subset of the twelve latches / eight pins still holds the door and pressure boundary with margin.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: In-flight release of the unsecured single-load-path nose visor causes forward-fuselage structural failure and explosive decompression (hull loss).
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The unaware SF-014-TL2 case couples loss of latching-and-locking with loss of both dissimilar lock-sensing paths, making it a significant latent failure.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The nose door lock indication guards a catastrophic un-secured-door condition, so its loss defaults to Major per §5.4.2.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Uncommanded or complete loss of longitudinal restraint on the single 72.6 t / 105 m blade produces a CG and/or wing-bending excursion beyond structural and controllability limits that the crew cannot arrest.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: After a partial restraint loss the blade remains geometrically restrained (no longitudinal travel) with the lost strap's load carried by neighbouring straps, and the condition is annunciated to the crew.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: An erroneous nose-door lock status indication can present a false-locked state, and the underlying door-open-in-flight condition it can mask (loss of pressure boundary / forward structural load path) is at least Hazardous.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: An undetected in-flight release of the single-item blade restraint progresses to a centre-of-gravity and hold-structure excursion the crew cannot arrest, because the crew has indication only and no in-flight adjustment.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Loss of a single strap load path is carried by its neighbours within the restraint design margin, keeping partial restraint loss at a significant rather than large reduction.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed erroneous detection can misdirect crew to shut down a healthy engine or misidentify the fire zone. Whether a mis-shutdown during a real fire escalates to Hazardous depends on the combination with an actual fire event and would confirm the class.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed crew act on the false warning (shutdown/discharge) per normal procedure; effect worst at take-off where a false-warning shutdown reduces margins. Phase-dependent effects could split this into a second row if a take-off inadvertent warning is judged Hazardous.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed 'undetected' means the loss of the detection function is itself latent (no annunciation of the failed detection), making it a significant latent failure that, combined with a fire, would be hazardous or catastrophic. Latency exposure and the combination probability with a nacelle/APU fire would confirm Hazardous vs Catastrophic.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed a nacelle/APU fire without any extinguishing can reach the wing fuel or primary structure before a diversion; the SDD states extinguishing is provided but does not bound propagation. Fire-propagation and diversion-time analysis (PRA/ZSA) would confirm or reduce this to Hazardous.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed 'partial' means loss of one bottle/one zone with cross-plumbing retained per §5.12.2; the FCIM does not bound which zones lose coverage. If a partial loss can disable both bottles of a pair simultaneously the outcome approaches the SF-028-TL case.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed the sizing case is a coincident depressurisation or smoke/fume event per §5.13.1; loss of oxygen alone in an intact cabin at FL260 or below has milder effect. If a coincident depressurisation is not credited concurrently, the standalone class may be lower; a combined pressurisation-loss FHA row would settle this.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed partial loss retains one cylinder via the crossover at reduced reserve per §5.13.3; the FCIM does not quantify the reserve remaining. If a partial loss can leave insufficient oxygen for the required diversion the class approaches the SF-029-TL hazardous case.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — SDD gives system function and redundancy (two cylinders, crossover, per-mask regulators) but does not substantiate detectability of erroneous delivery at the mask or its coincidence with an actual depressurisation. Assumed the error is detected at donning with a working alternate path (Major). Evidence that erroneous delivery could be undetected, or could coincide with a depressurisation with no alternate, would drive Hazardous (HAZ-2, crew unable to perform tasks).
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm
